question: Do Studio's engines reproduce the D5 Adobe oracle outputs for Illustrator (AI-01..05), InDesign (ID-01..04) and After Effects (AE-01..03)?
oracle: Handshake_Artifacts/WP-KERNEL-STUDIO/oracle-corpus/adobe-session/{illustrator,indesign,aftereffects} (session 2026-10-16, kernel 6912ce50: Illustrator 30.8.2, InDesign 21.6, After Effects 26.5); every file read is pinned by SHA-256 in its test
verdict_rules: MATCH within the stated tolerance; MISMATCH with deltas and diagnosis (a test fails on a MISMATCH not listed in its checked-in expected-mismatch file); NOT_SUPPORTED = no Studio engine for the case (measured delta reported); NOT_PROVEN = corpus file or variant absent. Never PASS: the round validator judges.
oracle_script_change: oracle-session/hsk_oracle_aftereffects.jsx AE-02: setSpatialTangentsAtKey now gets tangents padded to the Position value length (3 on AE 26.5). After Effects was NOT rerun; the AE-02 two_keys_spatial_tangents_set variant stays NOT_PROVEN until the lead schedules a run.

fixes: keyframe.rs: chord handle of a linear side inside a mixed linear/bezier segment uses influence 1/6 (was 1/3). Oracle AE-01b LINEAR_BEZIER and BEZIER_LINEAR: max error 2.69 deg -> 6e-10 deg.

assistants.rs make_continuous: the incoming speed wins (was outgoing). Oracle AE-01b chain3_continuous: setTemporalContinuousAtKey reads back in 20 / out 20 for in 20 / out 60; samples match to 9e-10. One key only: 'incoming wins' vs 'smaller speed wins' not separable (UNVERIFIED beyond this case).
findings: valueAtTime(t) is evaluated at t quantised to 1/1024 frame (24 fps comp: 1/24576 s); without modelling it the residual is up to 0.012 deg
Studio's normalised (time, value) cubic with 64-step bisection reproduces all 324 AE-01 segments (speeds 0/+-100, influences 16.67..75 %, influence sums above 100 % included) to 3.4e-9 deg
AE auto-bezier derives speed (v[i+1]-v[i-1])/(t[i+1]-t[i-1]) with influence 16.67 %: identical to Studio auto_bezier
default spatial (straight path, one path-speed ease) matches per-component evaluation to 0.0037 px (AE arc-length table)
AE roves along its spatial auto-bezier path: key 2 at 1.37679 s vs Studio's straight-line 1.37047 s; positions differ up to 11.7 px

illustrator.engine: hsk-studio-nib stroke outline / rasterize / paint_coverage; hsk-studio-pigment composite_over / evaluate_stack / knockout_over
findings: export pixel grid is anchored at the top of the artwork bounds (miter variants: 137 px, top = page y 136.154); bottom-aligned mapping misplaces every edge by 0.154 px

ARTOPTIMIZED = 4x4 point samples at sub-pixel centres, grey = round(255*(16-n)/16), plus an outward bias: 0.17 px on fills, 0.04 px on strokes (fitted on AI-02 fill_nonzero and AI-01 cap_round_join_round_miter1; the other 31 geometry variants are the independent check)

geometry through that sampler: dashes (3 patterns + offset + zero-length round dots), even-odd and non-zero fills and 14 cap/join/miter variants MATCH (max 32 grey, >= 99 % identical pixels, ink within 0.2 %); 9 butt-cap variants differ by up to 48 grey on the cap edge (Illustrator's butt cap ends ~0.1 px beyond the endpoint, Python fit) and 4 miter-limit-4/10 variants by up to 64 on the apex tip pixels (>= 99.58 % identical, ink within 0.18 %)
Studio's native exact-area raster vs Illustrator: ink 0.5 % (strokes) to 3.5 % (even-odd star) lighter, max 84 grey (no bias)

gradients: linear (50 %), radial, stop opacity over red MATCH within 1 level; midpoint 25/75 off by 40 levels: Illustrator's midpoint is a power curve (m > 0.5: t^(ln .5/ln m); m < 0.5: 1-(1-t)^(ln .5/ln(1-m)), fits 256/256 px to 1 level), nib skews piecewise linearly
16 blend modes x opacity 100/50 MATCH (32/32, max 2 levels) once the backdrop is the unquantised ramp (Illustrator blends above 8 bit: ColorBurn amplifies a backdrop step 12x)
isolation x knockout 4/4 MATCH with pigment evaluate_stack / knockout_over; Illustrator's knockout shape is the object coverage, object opacity is constant alpha (not shape)
antiAliasing None export: no aliased raster mode in nib (NOT_SUPPORTED; a 50 % coverage threshold agrees on 32655/32768 px)

indesign.engine: hsk-studio-interop-layout import_idml (InDesign's own ID-03 IDML) + hsk-studio-type shaping (rustybuzz, the exact Arial InDesign used) + hsk-studio-layout reflow_typeset
findings: glyph advances and kerning: every character x of every compared line agrees to 0.0000 pt except the 'ff' of 'differences' (InDesign f-f and f-e both 547 units, as if a 1094-unit pair split in half; Studio uses Arial GPOS f-f -37, f-e 0): 0.088 pt on that line
Single-line composer, ragged (left), no hyphenation: 10/10 widths identical line breaks
Single-line composer with hyphenation, left: 3/10 identical; the rest differ by hyphenation points (InDesign dictionary vs Liang patterns)

Paragraph composer: 4/40 identical (wide ragged frames); elsewhere Studio's TeX-model Knuth-Plass chooses different breaks and, when no break set meets tolerance 200, can put the unavoidable loose line first ('Ty-', 'Typographic' alone)

Justified variants: InDesign fits justified single-line-composer lines by shrinking spaces (ID-02 ws50: 44 chars on line 1 vs Studio 38) and always fills justified lines past the maximum word spacing; Studio keeps limits and reports residual_pt
hyphenateWordsLongerThan 5 behaves as 'at least 5 letters' (InDesign hyphenates 'ev-ery')
import_idml accepts all three InDesign-written IDML packages (48 typed loss entries each) and the imported story text equals the probe text byte for byte
ID-03 PDF exports are not compared (line data is compared through the JSON of the same documents)
